note: Arc mainnet, open since 2026-09-16. Named by chain id, which is the convention every chain after Arc testnet follows. Gas is USDC here as on Arc testnet, so an account pays for its own transactions in the money it holds. The consumer contracts are deliberately absent: escrow, the policy registry, the settlement vault and the yield adapter are the buyer-protection product and none of them is needed to hold, send or receive. A file without them parses, and the backend turns those jobs off rather than failing to boot.
verified: 2026-09-23, read off chain 5042 at head 22354417. The USDC precompile answers USDC. The Safe 1.4.1 stack, EntryPoint v0.7 and the Arachnid CREATE2 deployer all carry bytecode whose hash is identical to Arc testnet's, compared contract by contract. CCTP v2 is live: TokenMessengerV2 and MessageTransmitterV2 both carry code, which the roadmap had recorded as absent because it was written before mainnet opened. The RIP-7212 precompile at 0x100 returns 1 for a freshly generated valid P-256 signature, the same as testnet, so Face ID signatures verify on chain without a Solidity fallback.

safe.note: Canonical and audited, which is why the consumer account can be on mainnet without waiting for the Olien audit: Safe holds the money.

p256Note: Deployed 2026-09-29 in transaction 0x5ad33bba83ff09b457989e84c7c2e785cb11d68d8bb0970ec055c12e6c68217d, block 23283645, for 575,305 gas at 20 gwei, which is 0.0115 USDC because gas on Arc is the dollar itself. It landed on the address predicted from the salt and creation code before anything was sent. It is NOT Arc testnet's 0xBb27F2 and that is correct rather than a mistake: fallbackVerifier() reads zero here and Daimo's verifier there, because this chain answers the RIP-7212 precompile itself. The constructor argument is part of the creation code and therefore part of the address.

service.note: A second Railway service in the Recourse project, built from the same root Dockerfile as the testnet one, with its own Postgres (Postgres-Hals). It takes its chain entirely from DEPLOYMENTS_PATH=/app/deployments/5042.json, so no code distinguishes it. The boot log confirms what the file implies: no consumer contracts, so the escrow indexer, the resolver and the attestor stay off, and the treasury service is disabled because this chain has no Olien.
service.deposits: DEPOSIT_FACTORY=0x9C24d756781171e8839Ce0a5e37522BE5528FD82. The sweeper watches Base and reports the other seven chains idle rather than failing, which is the design: a chain listed but not deployed to costs nothing and starts working the day the factory lands there.
service.trap: A generated Railway domain comes with targetPort null and the service is unreachable until one is set. Same as the Monad service. railway domain update <id> --port 8080.
service.auth: Sign in with Apple, Google, passkeys, APNs push and the recovery vault are all configured, 2026-09-29. Two traps. The backend takes APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY_P8 as the PEM itself, not APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH, because there is no file in the image; backend/.env carries the path, so it has to be read off disk and piped in. And it refuses to boot when Apple is half configured rather than disabling it silently, which is correct but means setting the APPLE_* variables one at a time crash loops the service until the last one lands. Set them all, then redeploy.
service.recoveryVaultKey: Generated fresh for this chain, never shared with testnet, and held in backend/secrets/RECOVERY_VAULT_KEY.arc-mainnet, which is gitignored. It wraps every Recovery Key at rest and has no vendor side copy: losing it loses every sealed key, so a user who loses their phone loses their account. It costs nothing to lose today because nobody has sealed a key with it yet, and that stops being true with the first real sign up. Back it up off this machine.
